  89class ChartAxisOptions:
  90    """Class for defining the axis options for a chart."""
  91
  92    def __init__(self,
  93                 orientation: str = None,
  94                 min: Union[int, float] = None,
  95                 max: Union[int, float] = None,
  96                 date: ChartDateOptions = None,
  97                 title: str = None,
  98                 values: bool = None,
  99                 values_style: ChartTextStyle = None,
 100                 title_style: ChartTextStyle = None,
 101                 title_rotation: int = None,
 102                 major_grid_lines: bool = None,
 103                 major_unit: Union[int, float] = None,
 104                 minor_grid_lines: bool = None,
 105                 minor_unit: Union[int, float] = None,
 106                 formatCode: str = None):
 107        """
 108        Args:
 109            orientation (str, optional): The orientation of the axis, 'minMax' or 'maxMin'. Defaults to None.
 110            min (Union[int, float], optional): Minimum of the axis. Defaults to None.
 111            max (Union[int, float], optional): Maximum of the axis. Defaults to None.
 112            date (ChartDateOptions, optional): Date options, only for stock charts. Defaults to None.
 113            title (str, optional): Title of the axis. Defaults to None.
 114            values (bool, optional): Whether or not to show the values on the axis. Defaults to None.
 115            values_style (ChartTextStyle, optional): Styling for the values. Defaults to None.
 116            title_style (ChartTextStyle, optional): Styling for the title. Defaults to None.
 117            title_rotation (int, optional): Title rotation in degrees, clockwise from horizontal axis. Defaults to None.
 118            major_grid_lines (bool, optional): Whether or not to show the major grid lines. Defaults to None.
 119            major_unit (Union[int, float], optional): Automatic when undefined, spacing between major grid lines and axis values. Defaults to None.
 120            minor_grid_lines (bool, optional): Whether or not to show the minor grid lines. Defaults to None.
 121            minor_unit (Union[int, float], optional): Automatic when undefined, spacing between minor grid lines and axis values. Defaults to None.
 122            formatCode (str, optional): Format code for axis data, "General", "Number" ... Defaults to None.
 123        """
 124        self.orientation: str = orientation
 125        self.min: Union[int, float] = min
 126        self.max: Union[int, float] = max
 127        self.date: ChartDateOptions = date
 128        self.title: str = title
 129        self.values: bool = values
 130        self.values_style: ChartTextStyle = values_style
 131        self.title_style: ChartTextStyle = title_style
 132        self.title_rotation: int = title_rotation
 133        self.major_grid_lines: bool = major_grid_lines
 134        self.major_unit: Union[int, float] = major_unit
 135        self.minor_grid_lines: bool = minor_grid_lines
 136        self.minor_unit: Union[int, float] = minor_unit
 137        self.format_code: str = formatCode
 138
 139    @property
 140    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
 141        """The dict representation of these chart axis options.
 142
 143        Returns:
 144            Dict: dict representation of these chart axis options
 145        """
 146        result = {}
 147
 148        if self.orientation is not None:
 149            result["orientation"] = self.orientation
 150        if self.min is not None:
 151            result["min"] = self.min
 152        if self.max is not None:
 153            result["max"] = self.max
 154        if self.date is not None:
 155            result["type"] = "date"
 156            result["date"] = self.date.as_dict
 157        if self.title is not None:
 158            result["title"] = self.title
 159        if self.values is not None:
 160            result["showValues"] = self.values
 161        if self.values_style is not None:
 162            result["valuesStyle"] = self.values_style.as_dict
 163        if self.title_style is not None:
 164            result["titleStyle"] = self.title_style.as_dict
 165        if self.title_rotation is not None:
 166            result["titleRotation"] = self.title_rotation
 167        if self.major_grid_lines is not None:
 168            result["majorGridlines"] = self.major_grid_lines
 169        if self.major_unit is not None:
 170            result["majorUnit"] = self.major_unit
 171        if self.minor_grid_lines is not None:
 172            result["minorGridlines"] = self.minor_grid_lines
 173        if self.minor_unit is not None:
 174            result["minorUnit"] = self.minor_unit
 175        if self.format_code is not None:
 176            result["formatCode"] = self.format_code
 177
 178        return result

 181class ChartOptions():
 182    """Options object for a `Chart`."""
 183
 184    def __init__(self,
 185                 x_axis: ChartAxisOptions = None,
 186                 y_axis: ChartAxisOptions = None,
 187                 y2_axis: ChartAxisOptions = None,
 188                 width: int = None,
 189                 height: int = None,
 190                 border: bool = None,
 191                 rounded_corners: bool = None,
 192                 background_color: str = None,
 193                 background_opacity: int = None,
 194                 title: str = None,
 195                 title_style: ChartTextStyle = None,
 196                 grid: bool = None,
 197                 holeSize: int = None,
 198                 firstSliceAngle: int = None,
 199                 enableAreaTransparency: bool = None
 200                 ):
 201        """
 202        Args:
 203            x_axis (ChartAxisOptions, optional): The options for the x-axis. Defaults to None.
 204            y_axis (ChartAxisOptions, optional): The options for the y-axis. Note: date options for the y axis are ignored by the Cloud Office Print server. Defaults to None.
 205            y2_axis (ChartAxisOptions, optional): The options for the y2-axis. Note: date options for the y2 axis are ignored by the Cloud Office Print server. Defaults to None.
 206            width (int, optional): Width of the chart. Defaults to None.
 207            height (int, optional): Height of the chart. Defaults to None.
 208            border (bool, optional): Whether or not the chart should have a border. Defaults to None.
 209            rounded_corners (bool, optional): Whether or not the chart should have rounded corners. Note: displaying rounded corners is not supported by LibreOffice. Defaults to None.
 210            background_color (str, optional): Background color for the entire chart. Defaults to None.
 211            background_opacity (int, optional): The opacity of the background color for the entire chart.
 212                Note: backgroundOpacity is ignored if backgroundColor is not specified or if backgroundColor is specified in a color space which includes an alpha channel (e.g. rgba(0,191,255,0.5)).
 213                In the latter case, the alpha channel in backgroundColor is used. Defaults to None.
 214            title (str, optional): The title of the chart. Defaults to None.
 215            title_style (ChartTextStyle, optional): The styling for the title of the chart. Defaults to None.
 216            grid (bool, optional): Whether or not the chart should have a grid. Defaults to None.
 217            holeSize (int, optional): Hole size for doughnut chart (0-100).
 218            firstSLiceAngle (int , optional): Angle of first slice for dough chart (0-360). Must be specified for holeSize option to work
 219            enableAreaTransparency (bool, option): Whether to make area chart transparent.
 220        """
 221        self._legend_options: dict = None
 222        self._data_labels_options: dict = None
 223
 224        self.x_axis: ChartAxisOptions = x_axis
 225        self.y_axis: ChartAxisOptions = y_axis
 226        self.y2_axis: ChartAxisOptions = y2_axis
 227        self.width: int = width
 228        self.height: int = height
 229        self.border: bool = border
 230        self.rounded_corners: bool = rounded_corners
 231        self.background_color: str = background_color
 232        self.background_opacity: int = background_opacity
 233        self.title: str = title
 234        self.title_style: ChartTextStyle = title_style
 235        self.grid: bool = grid
 236        self.holeSize: int = holeSize
 237        self.firstSliceAngle: int = firstSliceAngle 
 238        self.enableAreaTransparency: bool = enableAreaTransparency 
 239
 240    def set_legend(self, position: str = 'r', style: ChartTextStyle = None):
 241        """Setter for the legend of the chart.
 242
 243        Args:
 244            position (str, optional): Position of the legend.  'l': left, 'r': right, 'b': bottom, 't': top. Defaults to 'r'.
 245            style (ChartTextStyle, optional): The styling for the text of the legend. Defaults to None.
 246        """
 247        self._legend_options = {
 248            "showLegend": True
 249        }
 250        self._legend_options["position"] = position
 251        if style is not None:
 252            self._legend_options["style"] = style.as_dict
 253
 254    def remove_legend(self):
 255        """Setter for removing the legend from the chart."""
 256        self._legend_options = None
 257
 258    def set_data_labels(self,
 259                        separator: str = None,
 260                        series_name: bool = None,
 261                        category_name: bool = None,
 262                        legend_key: bool = None,
 263                        value: bool = None,
 264                        percentage: bool = None,
 265                        position: str = None):
 266        """Setter for the data labels for the chart.
 267
 268        Args:
 269            separator (str, optional): Seperator : can be either false or anything else for example \n or \t or ; or (, if false). Defaults to None.
 270            series_name (bool, optional): Whether or not to include the series name in the data label. Defaults to None.
 271            category_name (bool, optional): Whether or not to include the series category name in the data label. Defaults to None.
 272            legend_key (bool, optional): Whether or not to include the legend key (i.e. the color of the series) in the data label. Defaults to None.
 273            value (bool, optional): Whether or not to include the actual value in the data label. Defaults to None.
 274            percentage (bool, optional): Whether or not to include the percentage in the data label. By default True for pie/pie3d and doughnut. Defaults to None.
 275            position (str, optional): The position of the data label.
 276                Can be 'center', 'left', 'right', 'above', 'below', 'insideBase', 'bestFit', 'outsideEnd', 'insideEnd'.
 277                Note that not all options might be available for specific charts. Defaults to None.
 278        """
 279        self._data_labels_options = {
 280            "showDataLabels": True
 281        }
 282
 283        if separator is not None:
 284            self._data_labels_options["separator"] = separator
 285        if series_name is not None:
 286            self._data_labels_options["showSeriesName"] = series_name
 287        if category_name is not None:
 288            self._data_labels_options["showCategoryName"] = category_name
 289        if legend_key is not None:
 290            self._data_labels_options["showLegendKey"] = legend_key
 291        if value is not None:
 292            self._data_labels_options["showValue"] = value
 293        if percentage is not None:
 294            self._data_labels_options["showPercentage"] = percentage
 295        if position is not None:
 296            self._data_labels_options["position"] = position
 297
 298    def remove_data_labels(self):
 299        """Setter to remove the data labels from the chart."""
 300        self._data_labels_options = None
 301

 352class Series(ABC):
 353    """Abstract base class for a series."""
 354
 355    def __init__(self, name: str = None):
 356        self.name: str = name
 357
 358    @property
 359    @abstractmethod
 360    def data(self):
 361        """Get the data used in the series. E.g. x-values, y-values, ..."""
 362        pass
 363
 364    @property
 365    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
 366        """The dict representation of this Series object.
 367
 368        Returns:
 369            Dict: dict representation of this Series object
 370        """
 371        result = {
 372            "data": self.data
 373        }
 374
 375        if self.name is not None:
 376            result["name"] = self.name
 377
 378        return result
 379

 381class XYSeries(Series):
 382    """A series for the case where the data consists of x-values and y-values."""
 383
 384    def __init__(self,
 385                 x: Iterable[Union[int, float, str]],
 386                 y: Iterable[Union[int, float]],
 387                 name: str = None,
 388                 color: str = None):
 389        """
 390        Args:
 391            x (Iterable[Union[int, float, str]]): The data for the x-axis.
 392            y (Iterable[Union[int, float]]): The data for the y-axis.
 393            name (str, optional): The name of the series. Defaults to None.
 394            color (str, optional): The color in which the series should be shown on a chart.
 395                Can be html/css colors or hex values. Defaults to None.
 396        """
 397        super().__init__(name)
 398        self.x: Iterable[Union[int, float, str]] = x
 399        self.y: Iterable[Union[int, float]] = y
 400        self.color: str = color
 401
 402    @property
 403    def data(self):
 404        return [{
 405            "x": x,
 406            "y": y
 407        } for x, y in zip(self.x, self.y)]
 408
 409    @classmethod
 410    def from_dataframe(cls, data: 'pandas.DataFrame', name: str = None) -> 'XYSeries':
 411        """Generate an XYSeries from a [Pandas dataframe](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.html).
 412
 413        Args:
 414            data (pandas.DataFrame): Pandas dataframe containing the data for the x- and y-axis.
 415            name (str): The name for the series.
 416
 417        Returns:
 418            XYSeries: XYSeries generated from a Pandas dataframe
 419        """
 420        x = list(data.iloc[:, 0])
 421        y = list(data.iloc[:, 1])
 422        return cls(x, y, name=name)
 423
 424    @property
 425    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
 426        result = super().as_dict
 427
 428        if self.color is not None:
 429            result['color'] = self.color
 430
 431        return result
 432

 434class PieSeries(XYSeries):
 435    """A series for pie charts."""
 436
 437    def __init__(self,
 438                 x: Iterable[Union[int, float, str]],
 439                 y: Iterable[Union[int, float]],
 440                 name: str = None,
 441                 colors: Iterable[str] = None):
 442        """
 443        Args:
 444            x (Iterable[Union[int, float, str]]): The data for the x-axis.
 445            y (Iterable[Union[int, float]]): The data for the y-axis.
 446            name (str, optional): The name of the series. Defaults to None.
 447            colors (Iterable[str], optional): Should be an iterable that contains the color for each specific pie slice.
 448                If no colors are specified, the document's theme color is used.
 449                If some colors are specified, but not for all data points, random colors will fill the gaps.
 450                The value for non-specified colors must be None.
 451                Warning: this is not the same as self.color of XYSeries, which is the color for the entire series, but this is not applicable to PieSeries.
 452                Defaults to None.
 453        """
 454        super().__init__(x, y, name)
 455        self.colors = colors
 456
 457    @property
 458    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
 459        result = super().as_dict
 460
 461        if self.colors is not None:
 462            # Add the color for each slice to 'data'
 463            for i in range(len(tuple(self.colors))):
 464                if self.colors[i] is not None:
 465                    result["data"][i]['color'] = self.colors[i]
 466
 467        return result
 468

 501class LineSeries(XYSeries):
 502    """A series for a line chart."""
 503
 504    def __init__(self,
 505                 x: Iterable[Union[int, float, str]],
 506                 y: Iterable[Union[int, float]],
 507                 name: str = None,
 508                 smooth: bool = None,
 509                 symbol: str = None,
 510                 symbol_size: Union[str, int] = None,
 511                 color: str = None,
 512                 line_width: str = None,
 513                 line_style: str = None):
 514        """
 515        Args:
 516            x (Iterable[Union[int, float, str]]): The data for the x-axis.
 517            y (Iterable[Union[int, float]]): The data for the y-axis.
 518            name (str, optional): The name of the series. Defaults to None.
 519            smooth (bool, optional): Whether or not the corners of the angles formed in the data-points are smoothened. Defaults to None.
 520            symbol (str, optional): Symbol representing the datapoints. Can be square (default), diamond or triangle. Defaults to None.
 521            symbol_size (Union[str, int], optional): Size of the symbol representing the data-points in (in em, pt, px, cm or in), by default: automatic. Defaults to None.
 522            color (str, optional): The color in which the series should be shown on a chart.
 523                Can be html/css colors or hex values. Defaults to None.
 524            line_width (str, optional): Thickness of the connecting line in em, pt, px, cm or in. Defaults to None.
 525            line_style (str, optional): Style of the line. Supported options can be found online on the Cloud Office Print documentation. Defaults to None.
 526        """
 527        super().__init__(x, y, name, color)
 528        self.smooth: bool = smooth
 529        self.symbol: str = symbol
 530        self.symbol_size: Union[str, int] = symbol_size
 531        self.line_width: str = line_width
 532        self.line_style: str = line_style
 533
 534    @property
 535    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
 536        result = super().as_dict
 537
 538        if self.smooth is not None:
 539            result["smooth"] = self.smooth
 540        if self.symbol is not None:
 541            result["symbol"] = self.symbol
 542        if self.symbol_size is not None:
 543            result["symbolSize"] = self.symbol_size
 544        if self.line_width is not None:
 545            result["lineWidth"] = self.line_width
 546        if self.line_style is not None:
 547            result["lineStyle"] = self.line_style
 548
 549        return result
 550

 552class BubbleSeries(XYSeries):
 553    """A series for a bubble chart."""
 554
 555    def __init__(self,
 556                 x: Iterable[Union[int, float, str]],
 557                 y: Iterable[Union[int, float]],
 558                 sizes: Iterable[Union[int, float]],
 559                 name: str = None,
 560                 color: str = None):
 561        """
 562        Args:
 563            x (Iterable[Union[int, float, str]]): The data for the x-axis.
 564            y (Iterable[Union[int, float]]): The data for the y-axis.
 565            sizes (Iterable[Union[int, float]]): An iterable containing the sizes for each bubble of the series.
 566            name (str, optional): The name of the series. Defaults to None.
 567            color (str, optional): The color in which the series should be shown on a chart.
 568                Can be html/css colors or hex values. Defaults to None.
 569        """
 570        super().__init__(x, y, name, color)
 571        self.sizes: Iterable[Union[int, float]] = sizes
 572
 573    @property
 574    def data(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
 575        return [{
 576            "x": x,
 577            "y": y,
 578            "size": size
 579        } for x, y, size in zip(self.x, self.y, self.sizes)]
 580
 581    @classmethod
 582    def from_dataframe(cls, data: 'pandas.DataFrame', name: str = None) -> 'BubbleSeries':
 583        """Generate a BubbleSeries from a [Pandas dataframe](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.html).
 584
 585        Args:
 586            data (pandas.DataFrame): Pandas dataframe containing the data for the x- and y-axis and the sizes for the bubbles.
 587            name (str): The name for the series.
 588
 589        Returns:
 590            BubbleSeries: BubbleSeries generated from a Pandas dataframe
 591        """
 592        x = list(data.iloc[:, 0])
 593        y = list(data.iloc[:, 1])
 594        sizes = list(data.iloc[:, 2])
 595        return cls(x, y, sizes, name=name)

 598class StockSeries(Series):
 599    """A series for candlestick charts."""
 600
 601    def __init__(self,
 602                 x: Iterable[Union[int, float, str]],
 603                 high: Iterable[Union[int, float]],
 604                 low: Iterable[Union[int, float]],
 605                 close: Iterable[Union[int, float]],
 606                 open_: Iterable[Union[int, float]] = None,
 607                 volume: Iterable[Union[int, float]] = None,
 608                 name: str = None):
 609        """
 610        Args:
 611            x (Iterable[Union[int, float, str]]): The data for the x-axis.
 612            high (Iterable[Union[int, float]]): The data for the hight prices.
 613            low (Iterable[Union[int, float]]): The data for the low prices.
 614            close (Iterable[Union[int, float]]): The data for the closing prices.
 615            open_ (Iterable[Union[int, float]], optional): The data for the opening prices. Defaults to None.
 616            volume (Iterable[Union[int, float]], optional): The data for the volumes. Defaults to None.
 617            name (str, optional): The name of the series. Defaults to None.
 618        """
 619        super().__init__(name)
 620        self.x: Iterable[Union[int, float, str]] = x
 621        self.high: Iterable[Union[int, float]] = high
 622        self.low: Iterable[Union[int, float]] = low
 623        self.close: Iterable[Union[int, float]] = close
 624        # open argument gets a trailing _ because open() is a built-in function
 625        self.open: Iterable[Union[int, float]] = open_
 626        self.volume: Iterable[Union[int, float]] = volume
 627
 628    @property
 629    def data(self):
 630        result = [{
 631            "x": x,
 632            "high": high,
 633            "low": low,
 634            "close": close
 635        } for x, high, low, close in zip(self.x, self.high, self.low, self.close)]
 636
 637        for i in range(len(result)):
 638            if self.open is not None:
 639                result[i]["open"] = self.open[i]
 640            if self.volume is not None:
 641                result[i]["volume"] = self.volume[i]
 642
 643        return result
 644
 645    @classmethod
 646    def from_dataframe(cls, data: 'pandas.DataFrame', name: str = None) -> 'StockSeries':
 647        """Generate a StockSeries from a [Pandas dataframe](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.html).
 648
 649        Args:
 650            data (pandas.DataFrame): Pandas dataframe containing the x, high, low and possibly volume and open data.
 651            name (str): The name for the series.
 652
 653        Returns:
 654            StockSeries: StockSeries generated from a Pandas dataframe
 655        """
 656        x = list(data.iloc[:, 0])
 657        high = list(data["high"])
 658        low = list(data["low"])
 659        close = list(data["close"])
 660        # volume and open are optional
 661        try:
 662            open_ = list(data["open"])
 663        except KeyError:
 664            open_ = None
 665        try:
 666            volume = list(data["volume"])
 667        except KeyError:
 668            volume = None
 669        return cls(x, high, low, close, open_, volume, name=name)
 670

 672# better to have a series for every possible chart for future-proofing, in case their options diverge later
 673BarSeries = BarStackedSeries = BarStackedPercentSeries = ColumnSeries = ColumnStackedSeries = ColumnStackedPercentSeries = ScatterSeries = XYSeries
 674RadarSeries = LineStackedSeries = LineSeries

 677class Chart(Element, ABC):
 678    """The abstract base class for a chart."""
 679
 680    def __init__(self, name: str, options: Union[ChartOptions, dict] = None):
 681        """
 682        Args:
 683            name (str): The name of the chart.
 684            options (Union[ChartOptions, dict], optional): The options for the chart. Defaults to None.
 685        """
 686        Element.__init__(self, name)
 687        self.options: Union[ChartOptions, dict] = options
 688
 689    @property
 690    @abstractmethod
 691    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
 692        pass
 693
 694    def _get_dict(self, updates: dict) -> Dict:
 695        """Update the given dict with the chart options and return the result.
 696
 697        Args:
 698            updates (dict): the dict that needs to be updated with the chart options
 699
 700        Returns:
 701            Dict: the input dict, updated with the chart options
 702        """
 703        result = {}
 704        if self.options is not None:
 705            result["options"] = self.options if isinstance(
 706                self.options, dict) else self.options.as_dict
 707        result.update(updates)
 708        return {self.name: result}
 709
 710    @property
 711    def available_tags(self) -> FrozenSet[str]:
 712        return frozenset({"{$" + self.name + "}"})
 713

1070def _replace_key_recursive(obj: Dict, old_key: str, new_key: str) -> Dict:
1071    """Recursively replace the keys in a (possibly) nested dictionary with a new name.
1072    Objects with key "options" will not be modified (y-axis stays y-axis).
1073
1074    Args:
1075        obj (Dict): input dictionary
1076        old_key (str): old name of the key
1077        new_key (str): new name of the key
1078
1079    Returns:
1080        Dict: input dictionary with the old key name replaced by the new key name
1081    """
1082    for key, value in obj.items():
1083        if isinstance(value, dict):
1084            if key != 'options':
1085                obj[key] = _replace_key_recursive(value, old_key, new_key)
1086        elif isinstance(value, list):
1087            for i in range(len(value)):
1088                value[i] = _replace_key_recursive(value[i], old_key, new_key)
1089    if old_key in obj:
1090        obj[new_key] = obj.pop(old_key)
1091    return obj
1092
1093
1094class CombinedChart(Chart):
1095    """Class for a combined chart. It is possible to combine more than 2 types of chart but there can only be two value axes."""
1096
1097    def __init__(self, name: str, charts: Iterable[Chart], secondaryCharts: Iterable[Chart] = None, options: ChartOptions = None):
1098        """
1099        Args:
1100            name (str): The name of the chart.
1101            charts (Iterable[Chart]): Charts for the first y-axis.
1102            secondaryCharts (Iterable[Chart], optional): Charts for the secondary y-axis. Defaults to None.
1103            options (ChartOptions, optional): The options for the chart. Defaults to None.
1104        """
1105        super().__init__(name, options)
1106        self.charts: Iterable[Chart] = charts
1107        self.secondaryCharts: Iterable[Chart] = secondaryCharts
1108
1109    def _get_modified_chart_dicts(self) -> List[Dict]:
1110        """Replace the y-axis with the y2-axis for the secondary charts.
1111        Add the dict representation for each chart to a list and return that list.
1112
1113        Returns:
1114            List[Dict]: list containing the dict representation for each chart, after processing
1115        """
1116        primary_list = list(self.charts)
1117        secondary_list = list(self.secondaryCharts)
1118        dict_list = []
1119        for chart in primary_list:
1120            chart_dict_full = chart.as_dict
1121            chart_dict = chart_dict_full[chart.name]
1122            dict_list.append(chart_dict)
1123        for chart in secondary_list:
1124            chart_dict_full = chart.as_dict
1125            chart_dict = chart_dict_full[chart.name]
1126            dict_list.append(_replace_key_recursive(chart_dict, "y", "y2"))
1127        return dict_list

182class ChartOptions():
183    """Options object for a `Chart`."""
184
185    def __init__(self,
186                 x_axis: ChartAxisOptions = None,
187                 y_axis: ChartAxisOptions = None,
188                 y2_axis: ChartAxisOptions = None,
189                 width: int = None,
190                 height: int = None,
191                 border: bool = None,
192                 rounded_corners: bool = None,
193                 background_color: str = None,
194                 background_opacity: int = None,
195                 title: str = None,
196                 title_style: ChartTextStyle = None,
197                 grid: bool = None,
198                 holeSize: int = None,
199                 firstSliceAngle: int = None,
200                 enableAreaTransparency: bool = None
201                 ):
202        """
203        Args:
204            x_axis (ChartAxisOptions, optional): The options for the x-axis. Defaults to None.
205            y_axis (ChartAxisOptions, optional): The options for the y-axis. Note: date options for the y axis are ignored by the Cloud Office Print server. Defaults to None.
206            y2_axis (ChartAxisOptions, optional): The options for the y2-axis. Note: date options for the y2 axis are ignored by the Cloud Office Print server. Defaults to None.
207            width (int, optional): Width of the chart. Defaults to None.
208            height (int, optional): Height of the chart. Defaults to None.
209            border (bool, optional): Whether or not the chart should have a border. Defaults to None.
210            rounded_corners (bool, optional): Whether or not the chart should have rounded corners. Note: displaying rounded corners is not supported by LibreOffice. Defaults to None.
211            background_color (str, optional): Background color for the entire chart. Defaults to None.
212            background_opacity (int, optional): The opacity of the background color for the entire chart.
213                Note: backgroundOpacity is ignored if backgroundColor is not specified or if backgroundColor is specified in a color space which includes an alpha channel (e.g. rgba(0,191,255,0.5)).
214                In the latter case, the alpha channel in backgroundColor is used. Defaults to None.
215            title (str, optional): The title of the chart. Defaults to None.
216            title_style (ChartTextStyle, optional): The styling for the title of the chart. Defaults to None.
217            grid (bool, optional): Whether or not the chart should have a grid. Defaults to None.
218            holeSize (int, optional): Hole size for doughnut chart (0-100).
219            firstSLiceAngle (int , optional): Angle of first slice for dough chart (0-360). Must be specified for holeSize option to work
220            enableAreaTransparency (bool, option): Whether to make area chart transparent.
221        """
222        self._legend_options: dict = None
223        self._data_labels_options: dict = None
224
225        self.x_axis: ChartAxisOptions = x_axis
226        self.y_axis: ChartAxisOptions = y_axis
227        self.y2_axis: ChartAxisOptions = y2_axis
228        self.width: int = width
229        self.height: int = height
230        self.border: bool = border
231        self.rounded_corners: bool = rounded_corners
232        self.background_color: str = background_color
233        self.background_opacity: int = background_opacity
234        self.title: str = title
235        self.title_style: ChartTextStyle = title_style
236        self.grid: bool = grid
237        self.holeSize: int = holeSize
238        self.firstSliceAngle: int = firstSliceAngle 
239        self.enableAreaTransparency: bool = enableAreaTransparency 
240
241    def set_legend(self, position: str = 'r', style: ChartTextStyle = None):
242        """Setter for the legend of the chart.
243
244        Args:
245            position (str, optional): Position of the legend.  'l': left, 'r': right, 'b': bottom, 't': top. Defaults to 'r'.
246            style (ChartTextStyle, optional): The styling for the text of the legend. Defaults to None.
247        """
248        self._legend_options = {
249            "showLegend": True
250        }
251        self._legend_options["position"] = position
252        if style is not None:
253            self._legend_options["style"] = style.as_dict
254
255    def remove_legend(self):
256        """Setter for removing the legend from the chart."""
257        self._legend_options = None
258
259    def set_data_labels(self,
260                        separator: str = None,
261                        series_name: bool = None,
262                        category_name: bool = None,
263                        legend_key: bool = None,
264                        value: bool = None,
265                        percentage: bool = None,
266                        position: str = None):
267        """Setter for the data labels for the chart.
268
269        Args:
270            separator (str, optional): Seperator : can be either false or anything else for example \n or \t or ; or (, if false). Defaults to None.
271            series_name (bool, optional): Whether or not to include the series name in the data label. Defaults to None.
272            category_name (bool, optional): Whether or not to include the series category name in the data label. Defaults to None.
273            legend_key (bool, optional): Whether or not to include the legend key (i.e. the color of the series) in the data label. Defaults to None.
274            value (bool, optional): Whether or not to include the actual value in the data label. Defaults to None.
275            percentage (bool, optional): Whether or not to include the percentage in the data label. By default True for pie/pie3d and doughnut. Defaults to None.
276            position (str, optional): The position of the data label.
277                Can be 'center', 'left', 'right', 'above', 'below', 'insideBase', 'bestFit', 'outsideEnd', 'insideEnd'.
278                Note that not all options might be available for specific charts. Defaults to None.
279        """
280        self._data_labels_options = {
281            "showDataLabels": True
282        }
283
284        if separator is not None:
285            self._data_labels_options["separator"] = separator
286        if series_name is not None:
287            self._data_labels_options["showSeriesName"] = series_name
288        if category_name is not None:
289            self._data_labels_options["showCategoryName"] = category_name
290        if legend_key is not None:
291            self._data_labels_options["showLegendKey"] = legend_key
292        if value is not None:
293            self._data_labels_options["showValue"] = value
294        if percentage is not None:
295            self._data_labels_options["showPercentage"] = percentage
296        if position is not None:
297            self._data_labels_options["position"] = position
298

300        """Setter to remove the data labels from the chart."""
301        self._data_labels_options = None

class XYSeries(Series): 
382class XYSeries(Series):
383    """A series for the case where the data consists of x-values and y-values."""
384
385    def __init__(self,
386                 x: Iterable[Union[int, float, str]],
387                 y: Iterable[Union[int, float]],
388                 name: str = None,
389                 color: str = None):
390        """
391        Args:
392            x (Iterable[Union[int, float, str]]): The data for the x-axis.
393            y (Iterable[Union[int, float]]): The data for the y-axis.
394            name (str, optional): The name of the series. Defaults to None.
395            color (str, optional): The color in which the series should be shown on a chart.
396                Can be html/css colors or hex values. Defaults to None.
397        """
398        super().__init__(name)
399        self.x: Iterable[Union[int, float, str]] = x
400        self.y: Iterable[Union[int, float]] = y
401        self.color: str = color
402
403    @property
404    def data(self):
405        return [{
406            "x": x,
407            "y": y
408        } for x, y in zip(self.x, self.y)]
409
410    @classmethod
411    def from_dataframe(cls, data: 'pandas.DataFrame', name: str = None) -> 'XYSeries':
412        """Generate an XYSeries from a [Pandas dataframe](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.html).
413
414        Args:
415            data (pandas.DataFrame): Pandas dataframe containing the data for the x- and y-axis.
416            name (str): The name for the series.
417
418        Returns:
419            XYSeries: XYSeries generated from a Pandas dataframe
420        """
421        x = list(data.iloc[:, 0])
422        y = list(data.iloc[:, 1])
423        return cls(x, y, name=name)
424
425    @property
426    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
427        result = super().as_dict
428
429        if self.color is not None:
430            result['color'] = self.color
431
432        return result

435class PieSeries(XYSeries):
436    """A series for pie charts."""
437
438    def __init__(self,
439                 x: Iterable[Union[int, float, str]],
440                 y: Iterable[Union[int, float]],
441                 name: str = None,
442                 colors: Iterable[str] = None):
443        """
444        Args:
445            x (Iterable[Union[int, float, str]]): The data for the x-axis.
446            y (Iterable[Union[int, float]]): The data for the y-axis.
447            name (str, optional): The name of the series. Defaults to None.
448            colors (Iterable[str], optional): Should be an iterable that contains the color for each specific pie slice.
449                If no colors are specified, the document's theme color is used.
450                If some colors are specified, but not for all data points, random colors will fill the gaps.
451                The value for non-specified colors must be None.
452                Warning: this is not the same as self.color of XYSeries, which is the color for the entire series, but this is not applicable to PieSeries.
453                Defaults to None.
454        """
455        super().__init__(x, y, name)
456        self.colors = colors
457
458    @property
459    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
460        result = super().as_dict
461
462        if self.colors is not None:
463            # Add the color for each slice to 'data'
464            for i in range(len(tuple(self.colors))):
465                if self.colors[i] is not None:
466                    result["data"][i]['color'] = self.colors[i]
467
468        return result

623        self.low: Iterable[Union[int, float]] = low
624        self.close: Iterable[Union[int, float]] = close

631        result = [{

637
638        for i in range(len(result)):

681    def __init__(self, name: str, options: Union[ChartOptions, dict] = None):

683        Args:

688        self.options: Union[ChartOptions, dict] = options
689
690    @property
691    @abstractmethod
692    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
693        pass
694
695    def _get_dict(self, updates: dict) -> Dict:
696        """Update the given dict with the chart options and return the result.
697
698        Args:
699            updates (dict): the dict that needs to be updated with the chart options
700
701        Returns:
702            Dict: the input dict, updated with the chart options
703        """
704        result = {}
705        if self.options is not None:
706            result["options"] = self.options if isinstance(
707                self.options, dict) else self.options.as_dict
708        result.update(updates)
709        return {self.name: result}
710

712    def available_tags(self) -> FrozenSet[str]:
713        return frozenset({"{$" + self.name + "}"})

1111        """Replace the y-axis with the y2-axis for the secondary charts.
1112        Add the dict representation for each chart to a list and return that list.
1113
1114        Returns:
1115            List[Dict]: list containing the dict representation for each chart, after processing
1116        """
1117        primary_list = list(self.charts)
1118        secondary_list = list(self.secondaryCharts)
1119        dict_list = []
1120        for chart in primary_list:
1121            chart_dict_full = chart.as_dict
1122            chart_dict = chart_dict_full[chart.name]
1123            dict_list.append(chart_dict)
1124        for chart in secondary_list:
1125            chart_dict_full = chart.as_dict
1126            chart_dict = chart_dict_full[chart.name]
1127            dict_list.append(_replace_key_recursive(chart_dict, "y", "y2"))
1128        return dict_list
